h1:
Santorini Park
White-and-Blue Greek-Themed Park, Cha-Am Hua Hin
intro: Drive north from central Hua Hin toward Cha-Am for about half an hour and you'll spot a cluster of white buildings topped with blue domes, as if someone lifted a village off the Greek island of Santorini and dropped it beside Phetkasem Road. This is Santorini Park, which packs a theme park, a Ferris wheel, a water park, shops and photo spots into one place that the whole family can enjoy. We've pulled together the latest details — prices, opening hours, the photo spots you shouldn't miss, and the things worth knowing before you go, told straight.

blocks.html: Santorini Park has been a photo landmark on the Cha-Am–Hua Hin side for years. The draw is its architecture, modelled on the cliffside villages of Santorini in Greece: crisp white buildings, deep-blue domed roofs, blue doors and windows that pop against the sky and make for a hugely popular photo backdrop. There's more here than just pretty corners, though — the grounds also include a rides zone, a water park, brand-name shops and restaurants. You can stroll through it comfortably in half a day.

blocks.text: What are the highlights at Santorini Park?

blocks.html: Roughly speaking, the park splits into a photo-and-shopping zone out front and a rides-and-water-park zone further in. Here's what most people don't miss.

items: Ferris Wheel — around 40m tall, this is the park's signature, visible from a distance. Ride up for a high view over the surrounding fields and the park itself; evening light is the prettiest.
White-and-blue Greek zone — alleys, stairways, balconies, a windmill and Mediterranean-style signage. You can wander and shoot from plenty of different angles without repeating yourself.
Alive Museum (3D illusion museum) — trompe-l'œil paintings that are fun to pose with, and a good pick on a scorching day since it's indoors.
Indoor and outdoor rides — there's a 4D X Ride, XD Dark Ride, a carousel, a haunted house, Water Ball, a trampoline and rides for little kids.
Santorini Park Waterventures water park — a water-park zone with several slides, ticketed separately from the main park, and a great way to cool off on a hot day.
Shops and food zone — clothing and footwear brands, coffee shops, and Thai, Japanese and snack spots where you can rest your feet.

blocks.title: For better photos
blocks.html: The white-and-blue buildings look best when the sun isn't too harsh — in the morning before 11am, or from late afternoon into the evening. The golden light against the white walls beats the midday glare, when the sun is so strong your shots blow out.

blocks.text: Ticket prices and opening hours (latest update)

blocks.html: Tickets here are split into separate parts rather than one all-in pass, so it helps to understand the system before you go and budget accordingly.

items: Walking and shooting the white-and-blue and shopping zone — you can enter this zone without paying an entry ticket; you only pay when you ride something or enter a ticketed area.
Standard rides — around 120 THB per ride, per person.
Special rides (XD Dark Ride 4D, Alive Museum, The Cage) — around 240 THB each.
Waterventures water park — a separate ticket, around 450 THB (full counter price; it's often cheaper if you book online in advance).
Opening hours — generally Mon–Fri around 9:30am–6:00/6:30pm; weekends and holidays open earlier, around 9:00am.

blocks.title: Straight talk on prices
blocks.html: Ticket prices and promotions here move around a lot depending on the season and where you buy. Some periods the water park runs a weekday deal at half price; other times the online tickets show up as Sold Out. So it's best to check the real price and the open status on the official page, or call ahead (032-772-999), rather than trusting prices from an old review.

Overall it's reasonably family-friendly, because there are rides for different ages — gentle ones for little kids like the carousel and a kiddie train, and slightly bigger ones like the 4D X Ride and the haunted house. Parents who don't want to ride can wander, take photos and wait at a café, while older kids who love the water can finish up at the water park in the same place.

items: Most of the walking surfaces are flat and stroller-friendly, but some spots are stairs and sloped photo ramps, so watch kids who run.
Shade in the outdoor zones is limited and the midday sun is strong, so bring a hat, sunglasses and drinking water.
If you're going to the water park, bring your own swimsuit and towel; there's a bag-drop and lockers in the water-park zone.
Long weekends and Saturdays–Sundays get busy and ride queues are long — if you want a relaxed visit, a weekday is better.

blocks.html: The actual location is in the Cha-Am area (Cha-Am district, Phetchaburi province), along Phetkasem Road on the Khao Yai–Cha-Am side, about 25–35 minutes by car north of central Hua Hin. People tend to lump it together as "Santorini Hua Hin" because most visitors stay on the Hua Hin side.

items: Private car / rental car — the easiest option, with a large parking lot. Just drop a pin on "Santorini Park Cha-Am" in Google Maps.

Taxi / hired car in Hua Hin — charter it round-trip or have it wait, and agree on the price before you get in. A round trip from Hua Hin usually runs into the several-hundred-baht range, depending on distance and waiting time.
Songthaew / Phetkasem-route buses — the cheapest option, but allow extra time and a walk at the end; good for those who aren't in a hurry.

blocks.title: Pair it up into a day trip
blocks.html: The Cha-Am–Khao Yai side has several photo-themed attractions and farms close together, such as the Swiss Sheep Farm and a vineyard. Do Santorini in the morning, then add one more spot in the afternoon, and you've got a tidy one-day family trip.

items.name: Windmill and blue-domed buildings
items.blurb: The classic shot everyone takes — the blue domes against the white walls and sky, and it frames up nicely in portrait orientation.

items.name: Stairways and white alleys
items.blurb: Walk up the narrow stairs between the buildings for a Greek-village-alley feel; great for full-length shots.

items.name: Ferris wheel from below
items.blurb: Stand so the full wheel is in frame; in the evening the lights come on and look great.

items.name: Alive Museum 3D
items.blurb: Indoor optical illusions for fun, playful photos — good for groups of friends and kids.

blocks.text: Santorini Park in half a day to a full day

items.activity: Arrive at opening and walk the white-and-blue zone while the sun is still gentle.
items.note: Fewer people, so you get clear shots.

items.activity: Hit the rides and duck into the Alive Museum to escape the sun.
items.note: Buy tickets only for the rides you'll do.

items.activity: Ride the Ferris wheel for the high view.
Break for lunch in the restaurant zone.
Head to Waterventures and ride the slides to cool off.
Shower, change, and browse the brand shops.
Move on to the Swiss Sheep Farm or a nearby vineyard for photos in the evening light.
items.note: Or head back into Hua Hin to find dinner.

faq.q: How much is admission to Santorini Park?
faq.a: Walking in to photograph the white-and-blue and shopping zone doesn't require an entry ticket for that zone — you pay per ride instead. Standard rides are around 120 THB each, special rides around 240 THB, and the Waterventures water park is a separate ticket at around 450 THB. Prices shift with the season and promotions, so it's best to check with the official page before you go.

faq.q: What time does Santorini Park open?
faq.a: Generally Mon–Fri it opens around 9:30am to 6:00–6:30pm, and weekends and holidays open earlier, around 9:00am. Closing times can change with the season, so check the latest before you travel.

faq.q: Is Santorini Park in Hua Hin or Cha-Am?
faq.a: The actual location is in Cha-Am district, Phetchaburi province, along Phetkasem Road on the Khao Yai–Cha-Am side, about 25–35 minutes by car north of central Hua Hin. People call it "Santorini Hua Hin" because most visitors stay in Hua Hin.

faq.q: Is it good for taking kids?
faq.a: Yes. There are rides for different ages, for both little kids and older ones, plus the water park and photo spots. Parents who don't ride can wander, take photos and wait at a café. But the midday sun is strong and shade is limited, so bring a hat and drinking water. Weekends get crowded with long queues, so weekdays are more comfortable.

faq.q: How many hours do you need to visit?
faq.a: If you focus on photos and a few rides, around 2–3 hours is enough. But if you're adding the water park, allow half a day to nearly a full day.
